Build the settings page

For a coding agent · 72 words

Build the Settings page for Your product in this codebase.

What it is for: let an owner rename the workspace and choose who can invite people.

Use only these components: page header (default), text field, segmented control, button (primary, quiet).
States: default, saving, error ("The name is already taken").

Done when:
- Every state renders and is reachable with the keyboard alone.
- No raw colour, size or duration values; every value comes from a token.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To offer a ready-to-paste instruction for an AI coding agent: build a component, implement a screen, fix a review comment.
  • ring where the page around it already says what the prompt is for, and handing it to an agent is the page's one obvious action: people copy it in one click, or view it whole from its menu. The ring marks that action in place of the primary fill.
  • default where people should read the prompt on the page before they copy it: the card shows its title, its meta line and the whole prompt.

When not to use

  • For a command people run in a terminal: use cmp-code-block (strong).
  • For short code inside running text: use the typography mono class.
  • For a message the person should read and act on themselves: use cmp-inline-alert.
  • For a short prompt inside a list of steps: a cmp-button with its with-copy parts, beside a visually hidden cmp-code-block, is lighter.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — a flush card: the header with the prompt's title, its meta line and Copy prompt, then the whole prompt in a flush code block. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • ring — the lightest form: no card, icon or words, only the split Copy prompt button inside a thin rainbow ring (--ds-color-ai-1 … -5) that turns once every --ds-motion-ambient at a constant speed (--ds-motion-ease-steady), with a soft glow of the same colours behind it (--ds-opacity-glow, --ds-blur-glow), the sign of something handed to an AI agent. It stands still in the still motion preset and under reduced motion. Its chevron opens a small menu with View prompt and Save as Markdown; View prompt opens the whole prompt in a dialog, Formatted by default with a Raw switch. The prompt is never shown on the page while script runs; without script it is.

Anatomy

Built from:

  • cmp-button, variant secondary with its with-copy parts — the one action, "Copy prompt": data-ds-copy, so cmp-code-block's script copies the prompt; ds-button__copy-icon, ds-button__done-icon and ds-button__label with its two ds-button__sizer spans, so it keeps its width while it says Copied or how to copy. In ring it also carries join-start and ringed.
  • cmp-code-block, variant flush — the prompt text, <pre class="ds-code-block__code">: in default shown under the header, in ring also compact, inside ds-prompt-card__text.
  • cmp-card, variant flush — the surface of default only: <section class="ds-prompt-card ds-card ds-card--flush" aria-label="Prompt: <title>">. ring has no card.
  • cmp-popover-menu, variant split (ring) — the chevron end of the split button (cmp-button secondary join-end ringed), named "More ways to take this prompt" by a visually hidden label; two items, cmp-button quiet: View prompt (data-ds-prompt-view) and Save as Markdown (data-ds-prompt-save).
  • cmp-dialog and cmp-segmented-control (ring) — the view, made by component.js on first use (with-view in the specimen): the dialog with the prompt's title and meta; in its actions a segmented control ("View": Formatted, Raw) and Copy prompt; in its body ds-prompt-card__view (the formatted prompt) or a code block with the raw text.

Own parts:

  • Root: <section class="ds-prompt-card …" aria-label="Prompt: <title>">. ring adds ds-prompt-card--ring, data-ds="prompt-card" (so component.js adds the view and the download) and data-ds-prompt-file="<name>.md" for Save as Markdown.
  • ds-prompt-card__header: ds-prompt-card__heading with ds-prompt-card__title and ds-prompt-card__meta, then the action. When the card is narrow, the button wraps below the title instead of squeezing it. In ring the heading also carries ds-visually-hidden, so the view and screen readers still name the prompt.
  • ds-prompt-card__actions (ring): the split button, Copy prompt and the menu's chevron.
  • ds-prompt-card__body (default): holds the code block.
  • ds-prompt-card__text (ring): the raw prompt, which every action copies. Visually hidden while script runs; shown under the button without script.
  • ds-prompt-card__formatted (ring, optional): a <template> with the prompt rendered at build time, for the view's Formatted. Without it the view shows the raw paragraphs.
  • ds-prompt-card__view: the view's Formatted body.
  • ds-prompt-card__source (default, optional, with-source): the last line, naming what the prompt was assembled from and its source fingerprint.

Accessibility

  • The prompt is a section named "Prompt: <title>"; its title is a heading at the level the page needs, visually hidden in ring.
  • The copy button's accessible name is its label. After copying, the label reads "Copied" and a polite live region says "Copied to the clipboard"; if the clipboard is blocked the text is selected and the label says how to copy it.
  • Ring: the menu is cmp-popover-menu's (Enter, Space or ↓ opens it, Esc closes it); View prompt opens a modal cmp-dialog named by the prompt's title, and closing it puts focus back on the chevron. The Formatted and Raw switch is a radio group named "View". Save as Markdown says "Saved" for a moment and announces the file name.
  • Prompt text keeps its line breaks and wraps long lines; nothing is cut off or scrolls sideways.

Interaction

  • The button answers hover and press with a colour change; after copying it keeps its size and place while its copy glyph cross-fades into a check and "Copied" fades in, over --ds-motion-settle (cmp-button with-copy), for a moment (int-01, int-03, int-05). The menu and the view open and close with cmp-popover-menu's and cmp-dialog's own easing.
  • Focus stays on the copy button after copying (int-02).
  • Ring: the ring turns slowly and never pulses or grows; under reduced motion and the still preset it stands still (int-04, int-06). The view remembers Formatted or Raw for the next time (in the browser, when it allows it); Copy prompt in the view copies the same raw text as the button's.

Contract

  • Parts: in default, a flush card (ds-prompt-card) with a header holding the prompt's title, a one-line meta under it and the "Copy prompt" button (a secondary button with a copy glyph, a check glyph and its words), then the whole prompt in a flush code block, then optionally a last line naming what the prompt was assembled from (ds-prompt-card__source). In ring, no card: only a split button, "Copy prompt" joined to a chevron that opens a small menu with View prompt and Save as Markdown (ds-prompt-card__actions), inside a thin rainbow ring with a soft glow of the same colours behind it; the title and meta are kept for assistive technology and the view but not shown, and the raw prompt is held unseen (ds-prompt-card__text). Ring's view is a dialog made on first use: the prompt's title and meta, a "View" switch (Formatted, Raw), its own Copy prompt and Close in the header, and the prompt in the body, either formatted as readable text (ds-prompt-card__view) or raw in a code block.
  • States: the Copy prompt button: default; copied (the check replaces the copy glyph and the words read "Copied" for about 1.6 seconds); blocked (the text is selected and the words say "Press Ctrl+C", or "Press ⌘C" on Apple devices, for about 4 seconds); its width never changes. Ring also: menu closed or open (cmp-popover-menu); view closed or open (cmp-dialog), showing Formatted (the default) or Raw, the choice remembered for the next time when the device allows it; Save as Markdown's words read "Saved" for about 1.6 seconds after saving; and the ring turning, or standing still under the still preset and reduced motion. Without script, ring shows the raw prompt under the button and hides the split button.
  • Inputs: a click or tap on Copy prompt, or Enter or Space on it, copies the raw prompt (in default the code block's text, in ring the held raw text); focus stays on the button. Ring: the chevron opens the menu with a click, tap, Enter, Space or ↓, with cmp-popover-menu's keys; View prompt closes the menu and opens the view, which closes with Close, Esc or a click on the dimmed page and returns focus to the chevron; choosing Formatted or Raw (click, tap or the arrow keys, as in any radio group) switches the body; the view's Copy prompt copies the same raw text. Save as Markdown saves the raw prompt as a Markdown file.
  • Events: copying puts the raw prompt on the device's clipboard and tells assistive technology politely "Copied to the clipboard" (or how to finish the copy when blocked); Save as Markdown hands the device a file named for the prompt (prompt.md when none is named) holding the raw prompt with a final line break, and tells assistive technology "Saved as <file name>". It raises nothing else to the screen around it; a script may open a ring card's view by name (dsPromptView(card, "formatted"|"raw")).
  • Geometry: default's header has --ds-space-3 above, below and on the right and --ds-space-4 on the left, with --ds-space-3 between the heading and the button, and the button moves below the title when the card is too narrow for both on one line; the source line has --ds-space-2 above, --ds-space-4 on its sides and --ds-space-3 below, in small mono text. Ring is as wide as its split button, never wider than its container, with the ring 2 × --ds-border-width thick around it and corners of --ds-radius-control plus that thickness; the glow is the ring blurred by --ds-blur-glow at --ds-opacity-glow. The ring's colours (--ds-color-ai-1 to -5, back to -1) sweep round its centre and turn clockwise, as seen facing the screen, from 0° to 360° about the axis that points out of the screen, one full turn every --ds-motion-ambient at a constant speed (--ds-motion-ease-steady), forever; under the still preset and reduced motion it stays at 0°. The view's formatted text is at most the readable measure wide, at --ds-text-size-md, with --ds-space-4 between paragraphs.
  • Looks: default is a flush card with a hairline under the header; the title is medium size and strong, the meta smaller and muted; the prompt is in a flush code block. Ring is the secondary split button on the raised surface, framed by the turning rainbow ring and its faint glow. Copied shows the check and "Copied" in the same place and width. See the specimen's default × default, default × copied, ring × default and ring × copied cells; the ring cells also show the view, opened in place (with-view).
  • Names: the prompt is known by its title, which names the saved file and the view's heading; nothing else crosses.
  • Focus: Copy prompt keeps focus while its words change; the menu and the view take focus as cmp-popover-menu and cmp-dialog do, and closing the view returns it to the chevron.

Content rules

  • Titles start with a verb and name the result: "Build the settings page", "Fix the empty state".
  • The meta line says who the prompt is for and its length: "For a coding agent · 72 words".
  • Prompts are plain text written for the agent, in the second person, with the rules and a "Done when" list.
  • Never edit an assembled prompt by hand on the page; change its sources and assemble it again.

Do and don't

  • Do keep one prompt per card and one copy button per prompt.
  • Do show the source line wherever a prompt was assembled from files, so people can tell when it is stale.
  • Don't truncate a prompt to make the card shorter; use ring, which names the prompt and shows it whole in its view.
  • Don't put more than one ring prompt in a view: the ring marks the one thing to hand an agent, as a primary button marks the one obvious action.
  • Don't add a second, primary button; the copy action is the prompt's only button, and ring's other actions live in its menu.
